stories.headline: Russian barrage kills civilians around Kyiv
stories.summary: CBC/AP report that overnight Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed at least 17 people and wounded more than 40. Ukrainian officials said the attack hit civilian warehouses, infrastructure and a railway station, renewing urgent calls for air-defence support.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray for Ukrainians living under routine terror, and for believers to be steady witnesses of mercy when grief becomes ordinary. This is a day to intercede for peace without growing numb to the human cost.

stories.headline: Sudanese parish mourns after attack and killing of priest
stories.summary: International Christian Concern reports that Upper Kauda St. Vincent Catholic Parish in Sudan's Nuba Mountains continues to grieve after a June attack that killed Pastor Youhana Al-Amin and others, injured church workers, and drove families from nearby communities amid looting and fires.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold Sudanese believers before the Lord today, especially pastors and families serving where the church is both sanctuary and target. Their suffering reminds us that the body of Christ is global, wounded and yet still witnessing.

stories.headline: Gen Z religion story is becoming more complicated
stories.summary: TIME highlights new polling showing the longstanding religion gender gap narrowing among Gen Z. Gallup data suggests more young men are saying religion is very important, while other researchers point to young women leaving religion in response to disillusionment and perceived sexism.
stories.pastoral_note: The cultural opening is real, but it is not simple. Churches should welcome spiritually hungry young men without ignoring the wounds and questions that are pushing many young women away.

stories.headline: Assisted-suicide and religious-liberty questions intensify
stories.summary: The National Catholic Bioethics Center's August 4 public-policy report notes that Carmelite sisters have sued New York over an assisted-suicide law taking effect August 5, arguing it would require healthcare providers to inform patients about and assist with the process.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a shepherding moment around suffering, autonomy and Christian care for the vulnerable. The church needs language that is both morally clear and tender enough for families facing end-of-life fear.

stories.headline: HBR: Invisible work is draining strong employees
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review's recent leadership coverage argues that the mental load carried by employees is often less about the amount of work and more about how work is structured and distributed. HBR frames this as a leadership design issue, not merely a personal resilience issue.
stories.pastoral_note: Church teams carry invisible work too: emotional labour, logistics, relational remembering and quiet follow-through. Good leadership names the hidden load and redistributes it with honour rather than letting faithful people burn out unseen.

stories.headline: BC PST change coming for non-residential real estate services
stories.summary: FVREB notes that beginning October 1, 2026, BC will apply 7% PST to certain non-residential real estate services, including commercial trading services, non-residential rental property management, and non-residential strata management. Residential, supportive housing and farm properties are excluded.
stories.pastoral_note: For churches leasing, managing or planning non-residential property, this is worth flagging early for boards and finance teams. Stewardship includes noticing quiet regulatory changes before they become budget surprises.

stories.headline: AI tools help get food to hungry families in Somalia
stories.summary: UN News reports that the World Food Programme is using HungerMap Live and AI-assisted analysis to identify areas of urgent need in Somalia before conditions deteriorate. In Burhakaba District, the data helped direct food assistance to 48,000 people and nutrition support to 3,000 women and children.
stories.pastoral_note: Not every technology story is dehumanizing. Used under the command of love, tools can help mercy move faster; this is a hopeful reminder to pray and work for wisdom-shaped innovation.

stories.headline: Canadian survey exposes doctrinal confusion inside evangelicalism
stories.summary: Christian Daily reports on the 2026 State of Theology Canada survey, which found many self-identified evangelicals confused on core doctrines, including original sin, the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the deity of Christ and the authority of Scripture.
stories.pastoral_note: The evangelistic edge here is not scolding but clarity. A spiritually open culture still needs a church that can lovingly explain who Jesus is, why grace is necessary, and why historic Christian faith is better news than vague spirituality.
